fixed: "Neighbor Roll Away" and "Partners roll away" now come in as a roll away with your neighbor or partner, instead of one where the neighbors roll each other away. "Neighbor rollaway w/ half sashay", as Caller's Companion writes it, now comes in as a roll away too, and a note like "(Robins roll R, Larks step L)" sets who rolls the others away. This applies to imports, to figures you type, and to figures Re-check unrecognized figures reads again; roll aways already structured in your collection are unchanged.
A box circulate on a line of its own, imported or typed, now includes its balance in 8 beats and leaves it out in 4. Before, a box circulate that did not say either way always showed a balance.
A Caller's Box line that names its subject in a leading bracket, such as "[Ones] Box circulate", no longer shows that subject as assumed.

changed: The shared figure recognizer, and the ContraDB dialect for a line with one dancer set, read a relationship that is the line's only dancer set as roll_away's whom, leaving who to the default with assumedSubject; the recognizer also reads "rollaway" and "w/ half sashay".

withBeatImpliedBalance sets box_circulate's balance from a whole line's beats (8: true, 4: false) when the line has no top-level `;`, in the Caller's Companion mapper, the Caller's Box per-line parse, reparseImportGapFigures and parseFreeTextFigureEntry.

The CallersBox per-role roll-away annotation fills who on the whom reading for any roll-away relationship and clears assumedSubject; it also reads a role-named note ("role2s roll R, role1s step L"). A leading bracket that fills who clears assumedSubject, and does not overrule an annotation's roller.
